claims.text: The nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst is a fully homogeneous, single-phase solid solution.
PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyzes ethanol oxidation through a 12-electron process.
PtPdRhRuIrOs has high durability during ethanol oxidation.
Atomic-scale homogeneous mixing governs the ethanol-oxidation activity of PtPdRhRuIrOs.
Atomic-scale homogeneous mixing governs the durability of PtPdRhRuIrOs.
Homogeneous multielement mixing creates distinct neighboring active-site ensembles with different local electronic structures.
These active-site ensembles modulate the adsorption energies of ethanol and its dehydrogenation intermediates.
Ligand and strain effects arising from near-equiatomic mixing tailor intermediate adsorption strength.
Tailored adsorption enables efficient ethanol dehydrogenation.
Tailored adsorption enables C–C bond cleavage and thereby the 12-electron oxidation pathway.
Sluggish diffusion in the high-entropy alloy suppresses nanoparticle coarsening and degradation.
Higher-temperature or longer-duration post-synthesis annealing will induce controlled partial elemental segregation.
Partial segregation reduces the electronic synergy produced by homogeneous mixing.
Partial segregation will shift ethanol oxidation toward a roughly four-electron pathway.
The individual constituent metals generally promote no more than a four-electron ethanol-oxidation process.
Partial segregation will diminish durability by enhancing nanoparticle coarsening.
Maximally homogeneous samples will have significantly higher ethanol-oxidation activity than segregated samples.
Maximally homogeneous samples will retain structural integrity and catalytic performance longer than segregated samples.
A 12-electron product distribution indicates full ethanol oxidation rather than accumulation of partially oxidized products.
The proposed mechanism applies specifically to nanoscale catalysts under typical electrochemical ethanol-oxidation conditions where high-entropy and sluggish-diffusion effects are relevant.
